title: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)

sections.label: Bus and train ridership low
sections.summary: LTA revealed average daily bus and train ridership hit an 11-year low, falling 34.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Earlier this month, the LTA revealed that the average daily ridership for buses and trains have hit an 11-year low, falling by 34.5%.

sections.label: Bus and rail losses
sections.summary: As of July 2020 all bus services operated in the red, and rail operators were already making losses before the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As of July 2020, all bus services were already operating in the red.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Even before the pandemic struck, just 3% or bus services here were able to generate enough fare revenue to cover operating costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In May last year, then transport Minister, Mr Khaw Boon Wan shared that rail operators were already making losses before the pandemic struck.

sections.label: Fare model viability question
sections.summary: A question asks the Minister to explain the viability of the current fare model given Government Budget constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can the Minister explain the viability of our current fare model, subject to our Government Budget constraints going forward?

sections.label: Balancing prices and sustainability
sections.summary: It states transport authorities must balance efficient and affordable prices with the financial sustainability of the system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: No matter the funding sources employed to cover public transportation costs, it is crucial that the transport authorities find the right balance between efficient and affordable prices and the financial sustainability of the system.

sections.label: Subsidies and MRT spending
sections.summary: The Government spends $2 billion yearly in operation subsidies and $60 billion this decade to expand and upgrade the MRT system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Two billion dollars in operation subsidies a year, not including capital cost expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Government is spending $60 billion this decade to expand and upgrade the MRT system in Singapore and this is over and above the $2 billion operational subsidies.

sections.label: MKBF improvement in 2020
sections.summary: In June 2020, the MKBF was 1,638,000 train-km, a 12-time improvement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In June 2020, five years later, the MKBF was an amazing 1,638,000 train-km – a 12-time improvement.

sections.label: Bus service profitability
sections.summary: Before the pandemic only 11 of 356 bus services were profitable, and by July 2020 all public bus services were in the red.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Before the pandemic, only 11 out of 356 bus services were profitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to MOT, as of July 2020, all our public bus services were in the red, meaning their fare revenue could not cover their operating expenses.

sections.label: Public transport utilisation targets
sections.summary: The passage asks what the targets are for public transport utilisation in five and 10 years and what measures MOT will implement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What are our targets for public transport utilisation, as compared to other travel modes, in five and 10 years' time respectively?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What measures and incentives will MOT implement to enable Singapore to reach these targets?

sections.label: Public transport investment viability
sections.summary: The passage asks whether public transport infrastructure investments will remain viable and financially sustainable given the pandemic and changed commuting patterns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In view of the pandemic and change in commuting patterns, will our public transport infrastructure investments still be viable and financially sustainable?

sections.label: Subsidy projections
sections.summary: The passage asks what the subsidy projections are for the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What are the subsidy projections for the next few years?

sections.label: Fare discounts for pre-informing
sections.summary: The passage states that commuters can be incentivised to pre-inform with discounts on fares.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Commuters can be incentivised to pre-inform with discounts on fares, for example.

sections.label: Aviation sector targeted support
sections.summary: The passage notes $870 million in aviation support and asks whether targeted support will extend to other affected aviation-related businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The aviation sector has seen the biggest influx of targeted support of $870 million in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: However, is the Ministry also looking to extend targeted support to other aviation related businesses that are similarly affected by the effective halt of air travel?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: It currently employs some 22,000 people of which 80% Singapore residents and contributed some $13 billion in total output to our national economy in 2019.

sections.label: Rolls-Royce and Eagle retrenchments
sections.summary: Rolls-Royce retrenched about 24% of its Singapore workforce in July last year, and NTUC intervened in Eagle Services Asia's retrenchment exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For example, the aircraft engine manufacturer Rolls-Royce retrench about 24% of its workforce in Singapore in July last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: NTUC itself had to intervene in the retrenchment exercise conducted by Eagle Services Asia to protect Singaporean jobs.

sections.label: Aviation worker income and retrenchment
sections.summary: Aviation workers face income loss and job risk into this year and next, and the speaker asks about redundancy rates and COVID-19 recovery grant take-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This is a especially pertinent as aviation workers are likely to continue to experience a dent in their incomes, not to mention face increased job risk, well into this year and next, even as other parts of our economy slowly start to pick up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask in terms of retrenchment in the sector, what percentage of the aviation and aerospace sectors has been made redundant and what percentage of this retrench group has benefited from the COVID-19 recovery grants?

sections.label: Passenger traffic plunge after border closure
sections.summary: Since the March 2020 border closure, passenger traffic fell from almost 69 million a year to under 3% of that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Since the imposition of border closure in March 2020, passenger traffic has plunged from pre-COVID-19 peak of almost 69 million passengers per year to less than 3% of that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Changi Airport was the sixth busiest international airport and the Singapore Airlines used to carry more than 36 million passengers per annum pre-COVID-19.

sections.label: SIA and Changi sustainability question
sections.summary: The passage asks how much longer SIA and the Changi Air hub can sustain if travel borders remain closed beyond this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One, how much longer can SIA and Changi Air hub sustain if travel border remains closed beyond this year?

sections.label: Maritime Singapore Green Initiative funding
sections.summary: Since 2011, $100 million was set aside under the Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, extended to December 2024 and enhanced to focus on carbonisation of shipping.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Since 2011, under the Maritime Singapore Green Initiative (MSGI), $100 million was set aside to promote sustainable shipping.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: This initiative was further extended to December 2024 and enhanced to focus on the carbonisation of shipping.

sections.label: Flexibility for P2P drivers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry would allow P2P drivers more flexibility to wait in taxi stand bays and around drop-off points at night.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider allowing for more flexibility for our P2P drivers, to allow them to stop and wait in taxi stand bays outside the designated waiting lots, and even around taxi drop-off points, during the night when there is no longer any traffic or road safety worries about parked taxis along the road.

sections.label: Support for taxi companies
sections.summary: The passage asks how taxi companies will be supported in shifting to more energy-efficient cars without burdening drivers with the cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share more and how taxi companies will be supported in shifting to more energy-efficient cars without the burden of this cost being put on our drivers?

sections.label: Young tertiary-educated P2P drivers
sections.summary: The passage asks how many tertiary-educated Singaporeans below age 40 drive P2P vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Specifically, how many young tertiary-educated Singaporeans below the age of 40 are driving P2P vehicles?

sections.label: Capping PHC numbers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOT would consider capping the number of PHCs as it has limited taxis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Would MOT consider capping the number of PHCs like what MOT has done to limit the number of taxis?

sections.label: Taxi and PHC numbers
sections.summary: The passage states there are 16,000 taxis and 50,000 PHCs today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Today, there are 16,000 taxis but there are 50,000 PHCs.

sections.label: Electrification creating jobs
sections.summary: The passage states electrification of land transport is expected to give rise to new jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: First, the electrification of our land transport system is expected to give rise to new jobs.

sections.label: MRT network doubling
sections.summary: The passage states the MRT network is expected to double to 360 km by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Second, our MRT network is expected to double to 360 km by 2030.

sections.label: Tuas Mega Port first phase
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry for an update on the Tuas Mega Port and whether its first phase opening this year is still on track.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Lastly, can the Ministry provide an update on the Tuas Mega Port and whether its first phase opening scheduled for this year is still on track?

sections.label: LTA EV charging regulation
sections.summary: LTA would take over regulation of Electric Vehicles and EV charging facilities from the Energy Market Authority, and is willing to set up regulatory sandboxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Before I end, we heard yesterday that LTA would be taking over the regulations of Electric Vehicles, or EV charging facilities from the Energy Market Authority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: With the change, we know the LTA is willing to set up regulatory sandboxes to facilitate the introduction of new charging solutions.

sections.label: Caring SG Commuters Committee
sections.summary: The Caring SG Commuters Committee was set up in 2017 to transform Singapore's public transport system and commuter culture into one that is more caring, welcoming and inclusive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Chairman, the Caring SG Commuters Committee was set up in 2017, to transform Singapore's public transport system and commuter culture into one that is more caring, welcoming and inclusive.

sections.label: Improving commuter experience benefits
sections.summary: Improving the commuter experience can convince more people to take public transport, reducing both traffic congestion and carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Improving the commuter experience can convince more people to take public transport, reducing both traffic congestion and carbon emissions.

sections.label: Reducing train and bus crowding
sections.summary: The passage states a third aim of reducing crowding on trains and buses so commuters can have a more comfortable ride with better safe distancing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, reduce crowding on trains and buses so that commuters can have a more comfortable ride with better safe distancing.

sections.label: LTA Silver Zone initiative
sections.summary: Apart from a clarification, the passage states the speaker would like to touch on one of the LTA initiatives, Silver Zone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Apart from this clarification, I would like to touch on one of the LTA initiatives, Silver Zone.

sections.label: Walkability of liveable city
sections.summary: The passage states that walkability is the key component of a liveable city.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, the key component of a liveable city is its walkability.

sections.label: Riders' long working hours
sections.summary: Some riders work more than 10 hours a day and make upwards of 30 deliveries a day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Some riders work more than 10 hours a day and delivering upwards of 30 deliveries a day.

sections.label: Union calls for rider safety
sections.summary: The union calls for better safety nets for riders, greater road harmony awareness, and better supporting infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: The union calls for better safety nets for our riders and for the Government to push for greater awareness for road harmony and to build better supporting infrastructures for our riders.

sections.label: Cyclist footpath safety measures
sections.summary: After a cyclist was jailed over a pedestrian's death, the speaker urges LTA to educate cyclists, step up footpath enforcement, install cameras, and widen and demarcate paths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In a recent court case, a cyclist was sentenced to one week jail after he crashed into a 53-year-old pedestrian, who subsequently died.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I submit that LTA can do more to educate cyclists who use the footpaths to commute to ride at a reasonable speed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Hence, I urge LTA to step up enforcement along the footpaths and to install more cameras to deter inconsiderate riders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Wherever possible, LTA should consider widening the footpaths or park connectors and demarcate one side for cyclists and one side for pedestrians.

sections.label: Container throughput 2020 comparison
sections.summary: In 2020, container throughput was only 1% lower than in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In 2020, last year, container throughput was only 1% lower than 2019, the previous year.

sections.label: Crew changes completed
sections.summary: More than 100,000 crew changes have taken place today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, more than 100,000 crew changes have taken place.

sections.label: Public transport modal share target
sections.summary: The government aims to raise peak-hour public transport modal share from 64% to 75% by 2030, spending over $60 billion on rail this decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In response to Mr Gan Thiam Poh, we want to raise mass public transport modal share during peak hours, from 64% now to 75% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Members have asked about the plans for our public transport system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But notwithstanding this, over this decade, we will spend more than $60 billion to expand and renew our rail network and we will open new stations or lines almost every year.

sections.label: MRT network expansion
sections.summary: The MRT network will grow from about 230 km today to 360 km in the early 2030s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: With all these projects, the Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) network will grow from about 230 km today to 360 km in the early 2030s.

sections.label: Thomson-East Coast Line cost
sections.summary: The Thomson-East Coast Line costs more than $25 billion to build.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Take for example, the Thomson-East Coast Line – that costs more than $25 billion to build.

sections.label: Rail and bus operating subsidies
sections.summary: Train fares do not cover operating costs, so the Government spends about $1 billion yearly on rail subsidies and another $1 billion on bus subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Train fares so far are not enough to cover these operating costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, the Government has been spending about $1 billion a year to subsidise rail operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The situation is the same for buses – Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat gave an update to the House recently.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, operating subsidy amounts to another $1 billion of taxpayers' funds every year.

sections.label: Downtown Line NRFF review
sections.summary: The Government will review the NRFF arrangement for the Downtown Line, which is still on NRFF Version One.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Recognising that the NRFF has evolved over the years, we will review the arrangement for the Downtown Line, given that it is still on NRFF Version One.

sections.label: Periodic fare adjustments
sections.summary: Fares will need to be adjusted from time to time, as before.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Second, like before, we will need to adjust fares from time to time.

sections.label: Changi passenger volume during COVID-19
sections.summary: When COVID-19 struck, passenger volume at Changi fell to 0.5% of pre-COVID-19 levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: When COVID-19 struck, passenger volume at Changi fell to 0.5% of pre-COVID-19 levels.

sections.label: Changi Airport city connections
sections.summary: Changi Airport is now connected to 66 cities, compared to 160 cities pre-COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Changi Airport is now connected to 66 cities around the world, compared to 160 cities pre-COVID-19.

sections.label: Sector job losses up to 3Q 2020
sections.summary: Based on the Labour Market Survey, up to 3Q 2020, the sector had lost 6,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Based on the Labour Market Survey, up to 3Q 2020, the sector had lost 6,000 jobs.

sections.label: Aerospace sector support tiers
sections.summary: The aerospace sector is now in the top tier, 30% for the next three months, then 10% for the following three months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The aerospace sector is now in the top tier, 30% for the next three months, and then 10% for the following three months.

sections.label: National daily testing capacity
sections.summary: Nationally, more than 60,000 tests a day can now be performed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Nationally, we can now perform more than 60,000 tests a day.

sections.label: Air travel bubble with Hong Kong
sections.summary: An ATB has not been launched, but an agreed text with Hong Kong exists and it can launch when conditions are right.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have yet to launch an ATB successfully.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But we now have an agreed text with Hong Kong and the ATB can be launched when conditions are right.

sections.label: Vaccination and travel restrictions
sections.summary: More scientific data will show how much vaccination reduces virus transmission, enabling fewer travel restrictions for vaccinated individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As more scientific data become available, we will be able to ascertain the extent to which vaccination reduces the likelihood of someone carrying the virus and passing it to somebody else.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And this will enable us to allow vaccinated individuals to travel with fewer restrictions, perhaps even without SHN.

sections.label: Air travel bubbles
sections.summary: An ATB combines identifying safe places and imposing test requirements, and will play a key role in safe opening this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For example, an ATB is a combination of identifying safe places and imposing test requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I see ATBs playing a key role in safe opening this year.

sections.label: Frontline workers vaccination rates
sections.summary: 92% of seaport and airport frontline workers have gotten their first dose, and 85% have both doses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, our frontline workers at the seaport and airport, are substantially vaccinated – 92% have gotten their first dose, 85% with both doses.

sections.label: Vaccines favour the fight
sections.summary: With vaccines, the fight is in our favour.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: With vaccines, the fight is in our favour.

sections.label: Port container throughput
sections.summary: Our port handled 36.9 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our port handled 36.9 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs).

sections.label: Tuas Port progress update
sections.summary: First phase of Tuas Port land reclamation will complete by end of this year, creating 400 hectares for 21 berths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Ang Wei Neng asked for an update on Tuas Port.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We are on track to complete the first phase of land reclamation works by end of this year, creating 400 hectares to support 21 berths and handle 20 million TEUs a year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: When Tuas Port is fully operational, it will be as large as two Ang Mo Kios and handle up to 65 million TEUs a year, 50% more than our current capacity.

sections.label: Growing International Maritime Centre
sections.summary: Singapore will grow its International Maritime Centre, aiming for $20 billion in maritime business spending commitments from 2020 to 2024 and more jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will further grow our International Maritime Centre and encourage maritime companies to expand their operations here, including maritime law and arbitration, ship management and marine insurance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We aim to bring in $20 billion in total business spending commitments from maritime companies from 2020 to 2024, and create more jobs and more opportunities for our people.

sections.label: Maritime Innovation and Technology Fund top-up
sections.summary: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore will top up $15 million to the Maritime Innovation and Technology Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) will top up $15 million to the Maritime Innovation and Technology Fund.

sections.label: New Maritime Leadership Programme
sections.summary: MPA will start a Maritime Leadership Programme to train up to 30 local maritime managers in its first two runs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MPA will partner the industry to groom a pipeline of future leaders for Maritime Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We are starting a new Maritime Leadership Programme to train up to 30 local maritime managers for the first two runs to hone their leadership skills, build global perspectives on key maritime issues and strengthen their business networks locally and abroad.

sections.label: LTA Transport Infrastructure Collaboration Panel
sections.summary: LTA will form a Transport Infrastructure Collaboration Panel and expand the lodgement scheme to simplify and shorten development plan approvals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In line with the SG Together movement, LTA will partner the industry to make its approval process more pro-business.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It will form a Transport Infrastructure Collaboration Panel with representatives from the Real Estate Developers' Association of Singapore, Singapore Institute of Architects and Institution of Engineers Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For example, it will simplify and shorten the approval process for development plans, by expanding the lodgement scheme to allow more categories of submissions to receive in-principle approval upon submission.

sections.label: Reviewing rules and regulatory sandboxes
sections.summary: The panel will review existing rules and set up regulatory sandboxes to support innovative ideas and new business models.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Next, the panel will review existing rules and set up regulatory sandboxes to support innovative ideas and new business models.

sections.label: Zero tolerance limits innovation
sections.summary: Zero tolerance for failure or fear of mistakes means zero capacity for innovation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: If we have zero tolerance for failure or if we are too afraid of making mistakes, we will have zero capacity for innovation.

sections.label: Driver relief payouts disbursed
sections.summary: The Government has disbursed over $155 million to over 50,000 drivers and over $500 million to over 57,000 drivers under SIRS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As of February 2021, the Government has disbursed more than $155 million in relief payouts to over 50,000 drivers through the SRF and the COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund (CDRF).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Additionally, the Government has disbursed more than $500 million to over 57,000 drivers under the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In fact, we have committed $116 million towards CDRF payouts between March and June 2021.

sections.label: E-scooter footpath ban safety
sections.summary: Footpath accidents involving motorised PMDs fell 79% between 2019 and 2020 to 30 cases, and new import controls will roll out in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Over a year has passed since we banned the use of e-scooters on footpaths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: I am pleased to inform Ms Yeo that footpath safety has improved considerably, with accidents involving motorised PMDs on footpaths falling by 79% between 2019 and 2020 to 30 cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: To further enhance safety, we will be rolling out a new import controls regime for personal mobility devices and power-assisted bicycles in the first half of 2021.

sections.label: Cycling path expansion plans
sections.summary: Cycling paths will expand from 460 km to 1,300 km by 2030, with 28 km added by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan will be glad to know that we are pressing on with our plans to expand cycling paths from 460 km to 1,300 km by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: By the end of this year, we will have added 28 km of cycling paths, in Bukit Panjang, Sembawang, Taman Jurong and Yishun, as well mature estates such as Ang Mo Kio, Bishan, Tampines, Toa Payoh.

sections.label: Bus lanes travel time savings
sections.summary: When completed, dedicated and continuous bus lanes will shave up to 20 minutes for bus commuters from the North to the CBD.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: When completed, it will shave up to 20 minutes for bus commuters travelling from the North to the CBD with its dedicated and continuous bus lanes.

sections.label: LTA possible projects engagement
sections.summary: LTA has identified some 60 possible projects to be implemented and has commenced engagement for five projects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: LTA has identified some 60 possible projects to be implemented and have commenced engagement for five projects.

sections.label: Reshaping streetscape beyond Civic District
sections.summary: The Government will work with the community to gradually reshape the streetscape in Sembawang, Bishan, Toa Payoh, Tanjong Pagar and Jalan Besar.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Looking beyond the Civic District, we will also work with the community to gradually reshape the streetscape in areas such as Sembawang, Bishan,Toa Payoh, Tanjong Pagar and Jalan Besar.

sections.label: Wider footpaths and cycling paths
sections.summary: Footpaths may be widened by paving over roadside parking lots, and some roads will become cycling paths, starting in Ang Mo Kio Street 22.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Local business proprietors have also said that they would welcome wider footpaths, so that customers can browse more comfortably in front of their shops.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We are studying widening the footpath by paving over some roadside parking lots, thereby creating a more pleasant walking experience for pedestrians.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We will implement this with water-filled barriers temporarily for several months and then take in community feedback for further refinements, before permanently widening the footpath.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Aside from walkability, we will also start to convert stretches of roads into cycling paths, beginning in locations such as Ang Mo Kio Street 22, to expand our network of cycling paths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And pardon the pun, the road ahead remains challenging.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But we will step up our efforts to transform our land transport system to become more inclusive and sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We will also partner the community to build a landscape of roads and paths that meets Singaporeans’ aspirations for a liveable and sustainable home.

sections.label: Active mobility safety rules
sections.summary: Bicycles on public paths need brakes, work riders need third-party liability insurance, and e-scooter and power-assisted bicycle riders must pass a theory test.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, the Government accepted Active Mobility Advisory Panel's recommendation that all bicycles must have brakes when used on public paths and roads.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We also mandated third-party liability insurance for active mobility riders who ride for work purposes, such as delivery riders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To further enhance path safety, we announced that e-scooter and power-assisted bicycle riders must take a theory test to ride in public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: With this, all riders will know the rules and code of conduct.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will release the test handbook in April and begin testing in mid-2021.

sections.label: May I have a seat please
sections.summary: The "May I have a seat please?" initiative will be made permanent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Today, I am pleased to announce that the “May I have a seat please?” initiative will be made permanent.

sections.label: Signals and station signage
sections.summary: About 1,300 signalised pedestrian crossings have audio-tactile signals, which will be enhanced, and Thomson-East Coast Line stations have bigger, clearer signages.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: About 1,300 signalised pedestrian crossings have audio-tactile signals to help the visually impaired pedestrians.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will work with MSF to enhance these, such as extending their operating hours.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: At stations along the newest Thomson-East Coast Line, we have also taken in feedback from focus group discussions to introduce bigger signages with better contrast, larger font sizes and clearer symbols.

sections.label: Covered linkways and walkability
sections.summary: Over $370 million was committed over eight years on covered linkways, and the Caring SG Commuters Committee is studying ideas, with recommendations due mid-2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: For example, we have already committed over $370 million over the last eight years on covered linkways and we will continue to enhance walkability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The Caring SG Commuters Committee is studying these ideas and I look forward to their recommendations due in the middle of 2021.

sections.label: Cycling path targets and repurposing
sections.summary: 28 km of cycling paths will be added by year end, the target is about 1,300 km by 2030, and 60 road repurposing projects are identified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, this is something which we will assess and we will discuss with the relevant stakeholders and other agencies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I did say that by the end of this year we would have added 28 km of cycling paths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The target is to have about 1,300 km of cycling path by 2030, about 10 years away.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, if you divide it, that is the pace.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But having said that, even now, we have identified 60 road repurposing projects.

sections.label: Fare increases and vulnerable groups
sections.summary: Fare increases have occurred over the years and will continue, with PTC to convene in the second half of the year, while vulnerable groups must be protected through fare concessions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I am merely mentioning that over the years, from time to time, there have been fare increases and that same system will continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And in the second half of the year, PTC will have to convene and have to consider.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But whenever there is a fare increase, should there be one, we must always protect the vulnerable groups, like the low-income, the students, the seniors, and fare concession is one way to do so.

sections.label: Port and maritime services roles
sections.summary: The port sector has traditional roles like crane operators and drivers, and new roles need different skills, while maritime services such as financing, insurance, legal and brokering grow alongside the port.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If you look at the port sector, this will be the traditional roles that we have, crane operators, drivers, but increasingly, we are also looking at new roles that we need different skills and different groups of individuals to come in to fill these roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Similarly, I think for the maritime services which actually go hand-in-hand with the port, because when we grow our port and shipping lines call at Singapore, they register their ships here with our registry, they base their headquarters – their regional and global headquarters – here in Singapore, we can then offer them all the other maritime related services – financing, insurance, legal, brokering and so on and so forth.

sections.label: Raising job quality through tripartite partnership
sections.summary: People may transit from engineering, finance or IT into this growth sector, and beyond creating jobs, raising job quality requires tripartite partnership to redesign and upskill jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, they may transit, for example, from engineering, from finance sector, from IT, and they want to now enter this growth sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It is not just the number of jobs – which is very important and we will try our best and we will try and create as many as we can – but in the end, it is also about whether we are able to raise the quality of jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This is something which is very crucial because it requires a strong tripartite partnership to work hand in hand with companies and the Labour Movement to be able to redesign the jobs and to be able to upskill the jobs.

sections.label: Timeline for fully electric public buses
sections.summary: A clarification is sought on when the Government envisages the public bus fleet going fully electric.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: The second clarification – I am not sure which appointment holder will answer this – but I will like to take an opportunity to ask, when does the Government envisage our public bus fleet going fully electric?

sections.label: Aerospace retrenchment and electric bus target
sections.summary: There has been some retrenchment in aerospace, MOT with EDB will work with the sector, and the public bus fleet target is 2040 to be fully clean energy, possibly advanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: That applies to the aviation sector, but I know your cut was actually on the aerospace sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I do not have the numbers for aerospace but talking to unions, there has been some retrenchment – not huge numbers, some.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MOT, together with EDB, will try our best to continue to work with the aerospace sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On public bus fleet, the target is 2040 to be fully clean energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But we just made a big push towards EVs, so maybe it can be advanced.

sections.label: Guarding Singapore as maritime hub
sections.summary: Singapore must continue to be on guard to maintain itself as a safe and open maritime hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Even so, we always continue to be on guard so that we can maintain Singapore as a safe, as well as an open maritime hub.
